newsitem.title: GERMANY: Commerzbank says sees 96 dividend unchanged.
newsitem.headline: Commerzbank says sees 96 dividend unchanged.

text.p: Commerzbank AG, Germany's third largest commercial bank, plans to keep its dividend unchanged this year to boost reserves, chief executive Martin Kohlhaussen said in a newspaper interview published on Monday.
Operating profit would show "good double-digit" percentage growth in the first nine months of 1996, Kohlhaussen told Frankfurter Allgemeine Zeitung.
But Kohlhaussen aimed to keep the dividend unchanged, the paper said.
"We will significantly increase the substance of the bank from this year's earnings, that also benefits the shareholder," Kohlhaussen said.

Commerzbank paid a 13.50 mark dividend per 50-mark share on 1995 results after paying 12 marks plus a bonus of 1.50 marks for 1994. The bank has since reduced the nominal value of its shares to five marks in line with other major German companies.
The bank publishes nine-month results at a news conference on November 5.

Analysts polled by Reuters expect the bank to post an operating profit after risk provisions of 1.8 billion marks, a year-on-year rise of 47.5 percent -- unchanged from the 47.6 percent growth reported after the first six months.
Forecasts for Commerzbank's operating profit range from 1.71 billion marks to 1.92 billion.
